instructions: Heat the oven to 200°F. Set a wire rack on a baking sheet and put it in the oven to keep the finished tacos warm.

Chop the shrimp into 1/2-inch pieces and pat them dry. Dice the poblano into small pieces, slice the onion thin and mince the garlic. Core and finely chop the tomatoes. Chop the cilantro until you have about 1/3 cup. Shred the cheese if it's a block. Cut the limes into wedges.
Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the poblano and onion and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft and lightly browned.
Add the garlic, oregano, coriander, cumin and salt. Cook for 1 minute, until it smells toasty.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until most of the liquid is gone.

Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until they're pink and opaque. Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the cilantro. Taste the filling. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Transfer it to a bowl and wipe the skillet clean.
Stack the tortillas, wrap them in a damp towel and microwave for about 30 seconds, until warm and bendy.

Brush one side of a tortilla lightly with oil. Flip it so the oiled side is down. Sprinkle 1/4 cup of the cheese over it, spoon 1/4 cup of the filling over half, and fold it closed. Press gently. Repeat with the rest.
Set the skillet over medium-high heat. Lay 4 tacos in it with the folded edges toward the middle. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheese melts and the underside is golden and crisp.
Turn them with tongs and a thin spatula. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden. Move them to the rack in the oven and cook the other 4 the same way.
Serve with the lime wedges and salsa.
method_notes: Lead is Camila Made's tacos gobernador (no rating shown; none of the versions read had 20 ratings): shrimp, poblano and tomato cooked down with spices, then folded into cheese-filled corn tortillas and crisped in a pan. Alecooks (no rating) uses a simpler base with butter, garlic and oregano and adds the shrimp last, which is the order used here to save a pan step. Zestful Kitchen (no rating) bakes the tacos on sheets at 450°F with a thicker tomato sauce instead of pan-crisping. Serrano chile is left out to keep the filling mild, and soy sauce (in Alecooks) is left out so it stays gluten-free. Honest total is 37 minutes, over the 30 minute target.
